parallel.requirements: Recognized Rust 2021, std-only implementation, std::env::args parsing, black-box executable probing, byte-for-byte output including trailing spaces, and Cargo project plus root test10.rs placement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation, build, verification, and delivery; a spawned child was assigned review/testing after the initial implementation existed.
parallel.implementation: Parent created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, src/polygon.rs, src/triangulation.rs, and test10.rs, then adjusted CLI overflow behavior after additional binary probes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent repeatedly rebuilt the Cargo project and copied target/release/test10 to /output/test10; child read and built in the same /output tree for review.
parallel.verification: Parent ran cargo test, release builds, and byte comparisons across no-arg, ordinary, invalid, whitespace, signed, and overflow-like inputs; child also ran comparison probes.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official artifact passed, but the review child never returned a final result and the child briefly consumed stale target/release output while source was changing.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, black-box, exact output, std::env::args, Cargo structure, and root test10.rs obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, direct rustc support, Cargo build, byte comparison, and final delivery without delegation.
serial.implementation: Created a module-organized Cargo project with cli, geometry, earcut, output modules and a root test10.rs that includes src/lib.rs by path for direct rustc compilation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the release target and separately compiled /output/test10 from root source, leaving both executable paths available for evaluation.
serial.verification: Compared the standalone executable against the C++ reference for default, 0, 1, +2x, and abc, then checked the Cargo-built binary on input 1.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished work is visible in the trajectory; the official evaluator passed all 37 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same prompt constraints, including Rust 2021, std-only, std::env::args, exact C++ output, black-box behavior, and /output layout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same constraints and explicitly planned to reproduce the executable behavior in a small Rust project.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both passed the same official 37-case evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent owned the implementation and verification while also spawning a review_test10 child after the files were in place.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: One actor owned probing, implementation, both build modes, comparison checks, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added a reviewer delegation; serial kept ownership local and sequential.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The review child understood it should inspect /output and compare against the C++ binary, but worked from the shared workspace while the parent continued changing files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent context boundary; the same actor carried the observed argv and output facts into implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced an inter-agent review boundary and shared-artifact state; serial did not need a handoff or cross-agent workspace contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote cli, polygon, triangulation, lib, and root binary files, then patched cli.rs several times to match overflow behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote cli, geometry, earcut, output, lib, and a root file using #[path = src/lib.rs] so standalone rustc worked.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented a black-box constant observed index result for this input family; serial additionally designed the root source for direct rustc compilation while parallel relied on the Cargo crate for root source.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for the review child, observed it was still running, then interrupted it and finalized without a child return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and closed after its own completed checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an incomplete child-result lifecycle; serial's result lifecycle was local and complete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and child operated in the same /output tree; the child tested target/release/test10 while the parent was still patching and rebuilding cli.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial generated and tested artifacts after its implementation write in a single actor sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exposed the child to a stale shared executable artifact; serial avoided that state by sequencing writes and checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent ran cargo test, rebuilt release, copied the binary, and compared many ordinary and overflow-style inputs before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial compiled with both Cargo and direct rustc and compared default, 0, 1, +2x, abc, plus a Cargo-release check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did more edge-case probing and still passed; serial performed fewer probes but had direct rustc verification that the parallel parent did not run successfully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent 216 agent seconds and 804367 total tokens, including child review and wait/interrupt overhead, before passing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent 159 agent seconds and 208099 total tokens, with no subagents, before passing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred substantially higher budget cost from the extra review branch, but it did not compromise the official outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed status.json evaluations for both modes report solution_passed true with 37 of 37 testcases passed. The material task-solving difference is process-level: the parallel run used a review child, shared build artifacts while source was still changing, then interrupted the child; the serial run kept build and verification in one local sequence and additionally verified direct rustc compilation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel parent produced a passing artifact after local rebuilds, byte comparisons, and copying target/release/test10 to /output/test10.
Parallel review child added process overhead and did not return a final review before interruption.
serial_contributors: Serial produced a passing artifact through a single actor sequence with direct rustc and Cargo build verification.
Serial avoided child handoff, wait, and shared-artifact review timing issues.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial root test10.rs was directly rustc-compilable by using a path module, while the parallel root test10.rs depended on the Cargo crate and the child's standalone rustc probe failed.
Parallel probed and adjusted overflow-style atoi cases more extensively than serial, but the official tests accepted both outputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are adverse process episodes only

candidates.reason: The parent itself owned and completed the implementation files before delegating review, so implementation was not unassigned.
There were no separately owned implementation components requiring an unassigned integration owner; the parent integrated its own modules.
The parent assembled and delivered the root executable by building release and copying /output/test10.
The parent retained end-to-end ownership of probing, implementation, rebuild, verification, and final delivery.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent probed and then implemented directly.
The parallel run did not delegate a separate investigation phase that delayed implementation; the child was a later reviewer.
The indispensable path stayed with the parent and completed; auxiliary review did not starve implementation or delivery.
Only one review child was spawned and the run finished well before the cell timeout; there was no collective fan-out budget exhaustion.
The child had a bounded review assignment, not a demonstrably overbroad implementation scope that left indispensable task work unfinished.
The review child understood it should inspect /output, compare the executable, and check migration requirements; no known requirement omission controlled its work.
The parallel plan did not split separately produced components with incompatible interfaces; the child reviewed the parent's implementation.
No known finding or constraint is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer between parent and child.
The child did not receive an overly large handoff that it failed to reduce; it actively inspected files and test behavior.
The stale state was an executable artifact consumed from the shared filesystem, not a transferred handoff or report describing obsolete workspace state.
No incompatible completed reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parent had non-evaluator build, unit-test, and byte-comparison evidence before finalizing, so completion was not based only on a partial artifact or workflow return.
No replacement or retry agent repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; the only child was a first review attempt.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent spawned a review child, waited while it remained active, then explicitly interrupted it before the child finished its last checks or returned a final review.
candidates.realized_consequence: The independent review result was lost before final delivery, leaving the parent to close only from local verification after spending wait/interrupt overhead.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child was not a completed verifier whose result was trapped; it was still active and was explicitly stopped.

candidates.reason: The parent already had and promoted a passing release binary; no complete candidate was left unpromoted at closure.
The parent rebuilt and reran comparisons after parser changes, rather than merging child work after verification without a post-merge check.
The child did not produce a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt.
The child was interrupted while active, so the direct lifecycle error is early termination rather than a completed verifier result failing to return.
The review child was optional verification and the parent continued with local verification; no required failed child implementation scope was abandoned.
No completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored; the child never returned a final result.
The parent did wait on the child, but the same episode is more directly described by explicit early interruption after observing the child was still running.
There were no competing source designs from different agents claiming overlapping behavior; the child reviewed rather than implementing an alternate component.
Only the parent edited src/cli.rs; the child observed the shared file changing but did not edit the same source file.
No agent replaced non-entry source produced or owned by another agent.
The parent copied the final executable, but no child-owned or concurrently used deliverable was overwritten in a way that changed final behavior.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree work or invalidated provenance.
The shared workspace caused stale-artifact consumption, which is captured more specifically as Artifact Leakage; no broader unowned write instability is needed.

The child consumed /output/target/release/test10 as a stable Rust artifact while the parent was still changing src/cli.rs, producing a false overflow mismatch and requiring a rebuild before the child could correct its finding.
candidates.realized_consequence: The child generated a spurious overflow mismatch against stale target/release output and spent extra review time rebuilding before clearing that false finding.
candidates.near_match_reason: The stale datum was a generated executable in a shared environment, not a summarized or transferred handoff between actors.
